clue.text: I objectively toss in sou for poor creature in church

indicators.note: in says the tossed coin goes inside the other piece

parts.note: the pronoun I in the objective case is me

indicators.note: to toss the coin is to throw it about, so its letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker flips a small coin into a church collection for a pauper.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou is an old French coin of small value. The definition rests on the saying 'poor as a church mouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'poor as a church mouse' makes this rodent the proverbially penniless creature of the church.

clue.text: A plant coining money over a sweet drink popular in US

definitions.text: A plant coining money over a sweet drink popular in US

indicators.note: over puts the plant word above the drink in this down answer

parts.note: a plant is a factory, and the factory that coins money is a mint; mint is also a herb, the other plant sense
a julep is a sweet syrupy drink

explanation.surface: A herb is placed on top of a sweet cocktail that Americans love.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means on top. The whole clue also describes the drink: fresh mint leaves on a sweet bourbon cocktail, famous in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: This bourbon cocktail with sugar and crushed mint leaves is a Kentucky favourite, especially at the Derby.

clue.text: Disquieting omens of what may spoil a beautiful road

definitions.meaning: bad portents that make one uneasy

definitions.text: what may spoil a beautiful road
definitions.meaning: unsightly roadside boards that mar a scenic route

explanation.surface: Worrying portents about the ruin of a lovely country road.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is foreboding indications; the second is literal: unattractive traffic signs spoiling the view.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad omens are unpleasant portents, and unsightly signposts literally disfigure a scenic route.

clue.text: Eastern worker uprising apt to be explosive

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue says the insect word is read upwards

parts.note: an ant is the standard crossword worker, from the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: An Eastern labourer's revolt threatens to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns ANT to TNA beneath E. The definition is a description of the Sicilian volcano, which erupts often.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano erupts frequently, so it is described by its tendency to blow.

clue.text: The shabby impostor who cleared the field

definitions.text: The shabby impostor who cleared the field

parts.words: The shabby impostor who cleared the field
parts.note: a ragged stuffed figure pretends to be a man and frightens birds off the crops

explanation.surface: A ragged con man sees off everyone in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared the field' sounds like winning a race, but it means scaring birds off farmland; the 'impostor' is a dummy dressed as a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy in old clothes poses as a person to drive birds from a crop field.

clue.text: U-boat's mail boss? Not a main one

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub
the person in charge of a post office

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a submarine's head of post outranks any naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like the sea a U-boat sails; it means principal. The official runs a branch office, not the head one.
explanation.definitionFit: This official runs a small branch office rather than a principal one, so is subordinate.

clue.text: Adventurous narrative shown in a fine picture

indicators.note: shown in says the answer is on display inside the following two words

explanation.surface: A thrilling story displayed in a beautiful painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic tale of great deeds and adventures, like the Odyssey.

clue.text: A foreign capitalist restored manor

indicators.note: restored suggests rebuilding, so the letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: An overseas financier has renovated a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' is not a financier but someone from a capital city, here Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Italian capital is, to a Briton, a foreign capital-dweller.

clue.text: See 20 down
Man-made thread with only thin end twisted

indicators.note: twisted says the letters are wrung into a new order
the end of the word thin is its final letter

explanation.surface: A synthetic yarn whose thin tip has been twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges ONLY to NYLO, and 'end' adds the final letter of 'thin'.
explanation.definitionFit: This polymer is a synthetic fibre spun into thread, so it is literally man-made.

clue.text: The right sort of robe for wetting the baby's head?

definitions.text: The right sort of robe for wetting the baby's head?

parts.words: The right sort of robe for wetting the baby's head?
parts.note: wetting the baby's head is a toast to a newborn, but here it is the christening water on the infant, and the robe is the christening gown

explanation.surface: Asks what to wear to the drinks party celebrating a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'wetting the baby's head' means drinking to a new baby; read literally it is water poured at a christening. A 'right' is also a rite.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a robe worn at a christening, where water is sprinkled on the infant.

clue.text: Dangerously placed when jury pointed Pa out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their original order

explanation.surface: A courtroom moment when the jury singled out father, leaving him at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges JURY POINTED PA.
explanation.definitionFit: To be placed in danger is to be exposed to risk or peril.

clue.text: Fair saint of Cornwall

definitions.meaning: St ___ is a Cornish saint who gives his name to a town near Land's End

explanation.surface: A fair-minded holy man from the far west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip, full of places named after obscure Celtic saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and righteous are synonyms, and the Cornish town St ___ near Penzance honours a little-known saint of the same name.

clue.text: Strange rough man to produce notes, when given some blows

definitions.text: produce notes, when given some blows

indicators.note: strange says the letters that follow are put into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An odd, coarse fellow can only be made to sing by beating him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges ROUGH MAN TO. The 'blows' are breaths into the instrument, not punches.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica sounds its reeds when the player blows air through it, so breaths make the notes.

clue.text: The burden we must bear, apparently

definitions.meaning: a burden is a duty or responsibility
split into two words it reads as '...', what we have to carry

explanation.surface: A complaint about the load we are all stuck with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags that the second definition reads the word as two, ON US.
explanation.definitionFit: A responsibility is a weight that rests on someone, and split in two the word says just that.

clue.text: Whether up or down this crossing looks flat

indicators.note: in a down entry, read upwards or downwards the letters are the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A railway crossing that looks flat from either direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same both ways; 'this crossing' hints at a railway crossing at road height.
explanation.definitionFit: Even, horizontal ground is flat, with no slope.

clue.text: An Indian class sat awkwardly in church

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of sat are arranged clumsily into another order

explanation.surface: An Indian student group sat uncomfortably through a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' turns SAT into AST, which goes 'in' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindu society is divided into hereditary social ranks, each a closed class.

clue.text: Lord Brougham's calling for the masses to reform saw a huge, trend

definitions.text: Lord Brougham's calling for the masses

indicators.note: to reform is to re-form, so these letters are shaped afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: A Victorian lord's name for ordinary people prompts a vast push for political reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges SAW A HUGE TREND. Henry Brougham, a 19th-century Lord Chancellor, is credited with popularising the phrase for the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a disdainful label for the common people, attributed to the Whig statesman Brougham.

clue.text: Scotsman installed in new chair with a classier style of 12 & 21

indicators.note: installed in puts the Scotsman inside the reworked chair letters
new says the letters of chair are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Mon is a traditional crossword term for a Scotsman, from Scots 'mon' for man

explanation.surface: A Scot is given a new chair, with a posher version of a mouth organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the chair letters, and 'installed in' sets the Scotsman inside them. The cross-reference 12 & 21 is the instrument at 12 across, and this is its more dignified name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the more formal name for the reed instrument also called a mouth organ, played by blowing.

clue.text: A course for motor-cyclists or hikers?

definitions.text: A course for motor-cyclists or hikers?

parts.words: A course for motor-cyclists or hikers?
parts.note: for riders it is an unpaved racing circuit; for walkers it is simply a muddy path

explanation.surface: Asks what sort of route suits both bikers and ramblers.
explanation.walkthrough: Speedway bikes race on an oval of cinders or earth, and an unpaved country path suits walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-surfaced oval is used for speedway racing, and an unsurfaced footpath is a walker's way.

clue.text: Dropped a sealed message into Her Majesty's red despatch-box?

definitions.text: Dropped a sealed message into Her Majesty's red despatch-box?

parts.words: Dropped a sealed message into Her Majesty's red despatch-box?
parts.note: the red box sounds like a government minister's despatch box, but it is a red Royal Mail pillar box marked with the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: Someone slips a confidential note into the Queen's state papers.
explanation.walkthrough: British post boxes are red and carry the royal monogram, so 'Her Majesty's red despatch-box' is any street pillar box.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting an envelope into a pillar box is the act of mailing correspondence.

clue.text: The time to expect most strikes in the day

definitions.text: The time to expect most strikes in the day

parts.words: The time to expect most strikes in the day
parts.note: strikes sound like industrial action, but they are the chimes of a clock, which reaches its daytime peak of twelve at midday

explanation.surface: When during the working day walkouts are most likely.
explanation.walkthrough: A striking clock chimes once per hour, so twelve o'clock in the daytime gives the most strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, when a striking clock chimes the most times during daylight.

clue.text: The upper part of Charles's principality ?

definitions.text: The upper part of Charles's principality ?

parts.words: The upper part of Charles's principality ?
parts.note: Charles, when this was set, was the Prince of a principality, and its upper part on a map is its northern region

explanation.surface: Asks which is the top half of the Prince's realm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Wales title was held by Charles; on a map the top of a country is its northern region.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern part of the principality is its upper region on a map, around Snowdonia and Anglesey.

clue.text: See 12 across
Measures taken in return of client's pets.

indicators.note: return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits within the run of letters across the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Precautions taken over the safe homecoming of a customer's animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of client's joins 'pets' to give SPETS, which 'return of' turns round to read the right way.
explanation.definitionFit: Actions taken towards an end are called measures, as in taking firm action against a problem.

clue.text: … but only half the basic cover needed for them

definitions.text: … but only half the basic cover needed for them

parts.words: … but only half the basic cover needed for them
parts.note: following on from steps, the basic cover is footwear at the base of the body, and a pair is needed, so one item is only half of it

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue, grumbling that only half the essential cover was provided.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to 22 across: for taking steps you need a pair of shoes or similar, and one of the pair is half that cover.
explanation.definitionFit: One item of sturdy footwear covers one foot, half the pair needed for walking.

clue.text: It's a turn-up for bubbly drinkers

indicators.note: a turn-up in a down clue turns the words upside down, so they read upwards

explanation.surface: A surprise for people drinking champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' (a British word for a surprise) here turns IT'S A upwards. 'bubbly' is sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This Piedmont sparkling wine is a fizzy drink, and bubbly is slang for such wine.

clue.text: Suspect money obtained from a quiet little mischief-maker

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
an elf is a small mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: Dodgy cash taken from a quiet, impish little troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dismissive term for wealth, especially ill-gotten gain.

clue.text: Reginald is Trustee to a royal record collector

parts.note: Reg is the short form of the name Reginald
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A man named Reginald is trustee to a monarch's archive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a collector of gramophone records; the official keeps the register of births, marriages and deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: This official keeps the register of births, marriages and deaths, so gathers and holds records.

clue.text: Heath confused CIA after : about-turn.

indicators.note: after puts the muddled agency letters behind the turned piece
turn says the word for about is spun round to face the other way

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: confused says the three letters are muddled into another order

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is baffled by American intelligence after a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British prime minister, but here heath is the plant. 'turn' reverses RE; 'confused' shuffles the agency's letters, which come 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: This genus name covers the heathers, low shrubs that grow on heathland.

clue.text: The way to drop clues when lying with thin disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters are rearranged to look different

explanation.surface: Advice on hinting at something while telling a poorly concealed lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguise' rearranges LYING and THIN; 'drop clues' means give hints, not let clues fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop clues is to suggest something indirectly, and the adverb describes doing it suggestively.

clue.text: Honest work a 4 down might do after one has 19

definitions.text: work a 4 down might do after one has 19
definitions.meaning: a sub-post office worker stamps a postmark on mail once it has been posted

explanation.surface: Plain-speaking about a post-office worker's next task once mail arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point to SUBPOSTMASTER and POSTED A LETTER: the clerk then marks the stamp to cancel it.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid people are blunt, and postal staff mark a stamp to show postage is paid.
